solution: The cubic has three distinct real roots (it changes sign on $(-3,-2)$, $(0,\frac12)$, $(\frac12,1)$), so the Vandermonde determinant $V=(b-a)(c-a)(c-b)\ne0$
solution_full: Let $p(x)=2x^{3}+3x^{2}-5x+1$. Then $p(-3)=-11<0$, $p(-2)=7>0$, $p(0)=1>0$, $p(\frac12)=-\frac12<0$, $p(1)=1>0$, so the three roots are real and distinct and the denominator is non-zero.
Numerator $N$: apply $C_2\to C_2-C_1$ and $C_3\to C_3-C_1$. The first row becomes $(1,0,0)$, so $N=\begin{vmatrix}b^{2}-a^{2}&c^{2}-a^{2}\\b^{3}-a^{3}&c^{3}-a^{3}\end{vmatrix}$.
Take $(b-a)$ from the first column and $(c-a)$ from the second: $N=(b-a)(c-a)\begin{vmatrix}b+a&c+a\\b^{2}+ab+a^{2}&c^{2}+ca+a^{2}\end{vmatrix}$.
Hence $\dfrac{N}{V}=ab+bc+ca$, and by Vieta's relations for $2x^{3}+3x^{2}-5x+1$: $ab+bc+ca=\dfrac{-5}{2}=-2.5$.
originality_note: New: the ratio of the determinant with powers 0, 2, 3 to the Vandermonde determinant is the symmetric function ab+bc+ca, evaluated through Vieta on a given cubic (way 5). Closest known: the identity det[[1,1,1],[a,b,c],[a^3,b^3,c^3]] = (a-b)(b-c)(c-a)(a+b+c). Different because: the missing power is the first, the quotient is e2 rather than e1, and the roots are not known explicitly.
blueprint_concepts: Special forms: circulant and Vandermonde determinants

concept_use.Special forms: circulant and Vandermonde: The denominator is the Vandermonde determinant (b-a)(c-a)(c-b), and the numerator, a Vandermonde-type determinant with powers 0, 2, 3, factors as the same product times ab+bc+ca.

stem_review: Read as a student: a, b, c are the three roots (distinct, so the denominator is non-zero); ratio of two written determinants; no ambiguity in the order of roots, since both determinants change sign together. Checked numerically with the actual roots: ratio -2.5. Answer -2.50, a negative decimal as planned. Changed: No change.
key_step: Factor (b-a)(c-a)(c-b) out of the numerator; the quotient is ab+bc+ca = -5/2.
justification: A known Vandermonde-type factorisation followed by Vieta; routine chain with one non-trivial algebraic step. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q12 (L2) as a routine numerical.
